blocks.value: The Shareholding Pattern shows who owns the company's shares. It helps investors understand which groups have confidence in the business.
Imagine This: A pizza is shared among family members, friends and neighbours. Looking at who owns how many slices tells you how ownership is distributed. Companies work in the same way.
Typical categories include Promoters, Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs), Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs), Mutual Funds and Retail Investors.
If promoters own 55%, FIIs own 20%, DIIs own 15% and retail investors own 10%, that is the company's shareholding pattern.
Changes in shareholding over time can provide useful insights into investor confidence.
